page: Microsoft Azure M96-48bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 1946.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core density of 40.54 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 4608 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable for block storage performance. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth reaching 4147.11 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 156.64 GB/sec. CPU performance is characterized by a Passmark CPU score of 67646.12 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2205.0, placing its single-core capabilities in the top tier. The processor's Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions support strong execution in extended instructions, as evidenced by a Passmark extended instructions score of 69362.33. However, while prompt processing for a 70B LLM model is strong at 28.01 tokens/sec, text generation speeds drop to an average tier of 3.54 tokens/sec, highlighting a performance tradeoff for large-scale generative tasks without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Given the massive memory capacity of nearly 2 TB alongside 48 dedicated vCPUs, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise workloads. It demonstrates strong database operations performance with a Passmark database score of 26776.79 and a Redis SET throughput of 66.02 million operations per second. These characteristics make the instance highly efficient for hosting large in-memory databases, complex enterprise resource planning systems, heavy data warehousing, and intensive text or image processing pipelines.
